claims.text: As-cast FeNiCrMn is a single-phase solid solution.
As-cast FeNiCrMn contains nanoscale lattice distortions arising from multi-principal-element chemical inhomogeneity.
The dynamic mechanical response of as-cast FeNiCrMn is primarily governed by thermally activated dislocation slip.
Local lattice distortions caused by chemical inhomogeneity modulate dislocation slip in FeNiCrMn.
Local lattice distortions produce a distribution of dislocation-pinning sites in FeNiCrMn.
At lower temperatures, insufficient thermal energy strengthens dislocation pinning and limits dislocation glide.
Stronger pinning at lower temperatures increases the yield strength of FeNiCrMn.
Lower temperatures suppress work hardening and ductility in FeNiCrMn.
Very low strain rates increase yield strength and reduce ductility in FeNiCrMn by limiting dislocation motion.
At intermediate or elevated temperatures, thermal activation enables dislocations to overcome lattice-distortion pinning sites.
High strain rates increase dislocation mobility and interactions in FeNiCrMn.
Dislocation entanglement contributes to enhanced work hardening and ductility.
Dynamic recovery contributes to enhanced work hardening and a favorable strength–ductility balance.
Elevated temperatures and higher strain rates increase the work-hardening rate and ductility of FeNiCrMn.
Under quasi-static room-temperature loading, FeNiCrMn has moderate yield strength and balanced ductility.
The proposed mechanism applies only while as-cast FeNiCrMn remains single phase and lacks coarse precipitates or substantial microstructural heterogeneity.
Secondary phases, precipitation, or substantial microstructural heterogeneity may cause the proposed mechanism to cease applying.
In situ TEM or DIC strain mapping can quantify the proposed changes in dislocation density and mobility across the test matrix.
